entries.text: I'm on the SOC team and just got an "abnormal user behavior" alert in Jira. List the open alerts briefly and tell me which ones look related.

args.jql: project = SOC AND labels = alert AND statusCategory != Done ORDER BY priority DESC, created DESC

entries.text:
Six open alerts in SOC (all in Backlog):

- **SOC-1** (High): Abnormal user behavior: spike in declined card payments, concentrated on Northwind Electronics and Contoso Gift Cards.
- **SOC-2** (High): Brute-force login attempts from external IPs against online-banking accounts, some followed by a successful login.
- **SOC-3** (Medium): Partner merchants Northwind and Contoso report bursts of small charges that look like card testing.
- **SOC-4** (Medium): Unusual session activity: some accounts may be transacting without logging in.
- **SOC-5** (Low): Settlement returns slightly above normal for partner merchants. The data has no merchant_name field.
- **SOC-6** (Low): Printer offline on floor 3. Not security-related.

**Likely related:**
- **SOC-1, SOC-3** are the same activity: same two merchants, same window, and card-testing bursts would explain the declines.
- **SOC-2, SOC-4** look connected: brute-force logins with some successes, followed by sessions transacting without login, suggests possible account takeover.
- **SOC-1 and SOC-2** may be linked too, if the compromised accounts are what's being used for the declined card payments. Splunk would confirm this.
- **SOC-5** may be a weak link (same partners, but no merchant field to tie it to the others).
- **SOC-6** is unrelated.

This is based on the Jira descriptions only. I haven't queried Splunk yet. Want me to check whether the SOC-2 accounts overlap with the SOC-1 declines?
Run the ML models in our saved searches against that Splunk data. For each one, say which model it applies and show the top rows it flags.
I'll list our `demo_*` ML saved searches in Splunk, then run each one and report what it flags.

args.query: | rest /servicesNS/-/-/saved/searches splunk_server=local | search title=demo_* | table title, search, description

entries.text: Two `demo_*` ML saved searches: `demo_ip_decline_outliers` (DensityFunction on declines by IP) and `demo_txn_amount_outliers` (DensityFunction on transaction amount). Running both now.

Two `demo_*` ML saved searches ran against last-7-day `demo_payments` merchant transactions. Enterprise Security models were ignored.

**`demo_ip_decline_outliers`** applies **`demo_ip_decline_model`** (DensityFunction) to declines by source IP.

| ip_address | txns | declines | users | avg_amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 203.0.113.178 | 214 | 214 | 40 | 13.18 |
| 198.51.100.23 | 207 | 207 | 40 | 12.97 |
| 203.0.113.45 | 179 | 179 | 40 | 12.78 |

Those three IPs are 100% declines, ~40 users each, and small ticket sizes. That matches **SOC-1 / SOC-3** (card testing at Northwind and Contoso).

**`demo_txn_amount_outliers`** applies **`demo_txn_amount_model`** (DensityFunction) to individual transaction amounts. Top 5 of 18:

| time (UTC) | user_id | merchant | amount | status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-16 18:48 | user_10285 | Litware Books | 2533.58 | approved |
| 2026-11-17 18:44 | user_10179 | Litware Books | 2301.96 | declined |
| 2026-11-11 19:10 | user_10278 | Northwind Electronics | 2035.24 | approved |
| 2026-11-14 04:59 | user_10169 | Adventure Works Outdoor | 678.00 | approved |
| 2026-11-16 22:10 | user_10164 | Litware Books | 545.42 | declined |

Those are large, mostly one-off amounts at mixed merchants, so they look like unusual spend, not the small-decline burst. They do not explain SOC-1 the way the IP decline outliers do.
Check the flagged IPs against the login and session data. If they're behind this, open a follow-up ticket to block them.
I'll search login and session logs for those three IPs, then open a follow-up ticket only if they show up in the attack.

args.query: index=demo_payments sourcetype=authentication src_ip IN (203.0.113.178, 198.51.100.23, 203.0.113.45) | stats count AS attempts count(eval(action="failure" OR action="failed" OR action="fail")) AS failures count(eval(action="success" OR action="successs")) AS successes dc(user_id) AS users BY src_ip, action | sort - attempts

index=demo_payments sourcetype=user_access src_ip IN (203.0.113.178, 198.51.100.23, 203.0.113.45) | stats count AS sessions dc(user_id) AS users dc(session_id) AS session_ids values(page) AS pages BY src_ip | sort - sessions

entries.text: Auth: those IPs have ~895 failed logins and 5 successes. Session search on `src_ip` returned 0 rows — checking field names and which accounts succeeded.

args.query: index=demo_payments sourcetype=user_access | fieldsummary | table field, count, distinct_count, values
index=demo_payments sourcetype=authentication src_ip IN (203.0.113.178, 198.51.100.23, 203.0.113.45) action=success | table _time, user_id, src_ip, action | sort _time

index=demo_payments sourcetype=user_access user_id IN (user_10010, user_10021, user_10016, user_10012, user_10014) | stats count AS events dc(src_ip) AS ips dc(session_id) AS sessions values(page) AS pages BY user_id

index=demo_payments sourcetype=merchant_transactions ip_address IN (203.0.113.178, 198.51.100.23, 203.0.113.45) | stats count AS txns count(eval(status="declined")) AS declines dc(user_id) AS users values(merchant_name) AS merchants BY ip_address

entries.text: Confirming search: 895 failed logins and 5 successes from the three IPs; 600 declined card txns at Northwind and Contoso. Opening the follow-up ticket to block them.

entries.command:
acli jira workitem create --project SOC --type Task --summary 'Block card-testing and brute-force source IPs' --description 'Follow-up to SOC-1 (abnormal declined card payments), SOC-2 (brute-force logins), and SOC-3 (partner card-testing complaints).

Request: block these three source IPs at the edge / WAF / payment gateway:

- 203.0.113.178
- 198.51.100.23
- 203.0.113.45

Evidence (demo_payments, last 7 days):
- merchant_transactions: 214/214, 207/207, and 179/179 declines from these IPs (100% decline rate), 40 users each, merchants Northwind Electronics and Contoso Gift Cards. Flagged by demo_ip_decline_model.
- authentication: 292+299+304 failures and 5 successes (user_10010, user_10012, user_10014, user_10016, user_10021).
- user_access: these IPs do not appear as src_ip on portal sessions; the five compromised accounts still have transfer/view_balance sessions from other IPs.

SOC-4 (unusual session activity) is related but the block request is for the three attack IPs above.' --label follow-up
entries.result:
CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED: acli jira workitem create requires confirmation.
Rerun the same command with --yes after approval.

entries.text:
Those three IPs are behind this.

**Auth (`authentication`):** 895 failed logins and **5 successes** — `user_10010`, `user_10012`, `user_10014`, `user_10016`, `user_10021`.

**Payments:** 600 declined charges, 100% decline rate, only at Northwind Electronics and Contoso Gift Cards.

**Sessions (`user_access`):** the attack IPs never show as `src_ip`. The five accounts still have `login` / `transfer` / `view_balance` sessions from other IPs, so portal sessions are not coming from the same addresses as the card testing.

I am ready to open a follow-up task in SOC to block:

- `203.0.113.178`
- `198.51.100.23`
- `203.0.113.45`

entries.text:
I created [SOC-9](https://jirademosi.example.net/browse/SOC-9), "Block card-testing and brute-force source IPs", once, using the exact command you approved. It's labeled `follow-up`, references SOC-1, SOC-2 and SOC-3, and asks to block `203.0.113.178`, `198.51.100.23` and `203.0.113.45`.

Blocking the IPs won't secure the five accounts these IPs logged into successfully: `user_10010`, `user_10012`, `user_10014`, `user_10016` and `user_10021`. Those accounts are still active from other IPs, so they may need a password reset or session revocation. I can open a separate follow-up for that if you want.
